T1020.subject: C0001
T1020.text: During Frankenstein, the threat actors collected information via Empire, which was automatically sent back to the adversary's C2.

T1020.subject: C0046
T1020.text: ArcaneDoor included scripted exfiltration of collected data.

T1020.subject: C0059
T1020.text: During Salesforce Data Exfiltration, threat actors used API queries to automatically exfiltrate large volumes of data.

T1020.subject: G0004
T1020.text: Ke3chang has performed frequent and scheduled data exfiltration from compromised networks.

T1020.subject: G0047
T1020.text: Gamaredon Group has used modules that automatically upload gathered documents to the C2 server.

T1020.subject: G0081
T1020.text: Tropic Trooper has used a copy function to automatically exfiltrate sensitive data from air-gapped systems using USB storage.

T1020.subject: G0094
T1020.text: Kimsuky has exfiltrated data to C2 servers using an automated script that executes every 10 minutes and after successful checks for the presence of pre-designated staged filenames.

T1020.subject: G0121
T1020.text: Sidewinder has configured tools to automatically send collected files to attacker controlled servers.

T1020.subject: G1035
T1020.text: Winter Vivern delivered a PowerShell script capable of recursively scanning victim machines looking for various file types before exfiltrating identified files via HTTP.

T1020.subject: G1039
T1020.text: RedCurl has used batch scripts to exfiltrate data.

T1020.subject: S0050
T1020.text: CosmicDuke exfiltrates collected files automatically over FTP to remote servers.

T1020.subject: S0090
T1020.text: Rover automatically searches for files on local drives based on a predefined list of file extensions and sends them to the command and control server every 60 minutes. Rover also automatically sends keylogger files and screenshots to the C2 server on a regular timeframe.

T1020.subject: S0131
T1020.text: When a document is found matching one of the extensions in the configuration, TINYTYPHON uploads it to the C2 server.

T1020.subject: S0136
T1020.text: USBStealer automatically exfiltrates collected files via removable media when an infected device connects to an air-gapped victim machine after initially being connected to an internet-enabled victim machine.

T1020.subject: S0363
T1020.text: Empire has the ability to automatically send collected data back to the threat actors' C2.

T1020.subject: S0377
T1020.text: If credentials are not collected for two weeks, Ebury encrypts the credentials using a public key and sends them via UDP to an IP address located in the DNS TXT record.

T1020.subject: S0395
T1020.text: LightNeuron can be configured to automatically exfiltrate files under a specified directory.

T1020.subject: S0409
T1020.text: Machete’s collected files are exfiltrated automatically to remote servers.

T1020.subject: S0438
T1020.text: Attor has a file uploader plugin that automatically exfiltrates the collected data and log files to the C2 server.

T1020.subject: S0445
T1020.text: ShimRatReporter sent collected system and network information compiled into a report to an adversary-controlled C2.

T1020.subject: S0467
T1020.text: TajMahal has the ability to manage an automated queue of egress files and commands sent to its C2.

T1020.subject: S0491
T1020.text: StrongPity can automatically exfiltrate collected documents to the C2 server.

T1020.subject: S0538
T1020.text: Crutch has automatically exfiltrated stolen files to Dropbox.

T1020.subject: S0600
T1020.text: Doki has used a script that gathers information from a hardcoded list of IP addresses and uploads to an Ngrok URL.

T1020.subject: S0643
T1020.text: Peppy has the ability to automatically exfiltrate files and keylogs.

T1020.subject: S1017
T1020.text: OutSteel can automatically upload collected files to its C2 server.

T1020.subject: S1148
T1020.text: Raccoon Stealer will automatically collect and exfiltrate data identified in received configuration files from command and control nodes.

T1020.subject: S1166
T1020.text: Solar can automatically exfitrate files from compromised systems.

T1020.subject: S1183
T1020.text: StrelaStealer automatically sends gathered email credentials following collection to command and control servers via HTTP POST.

T1020.subject: S1211
T1020.text: Hannotog can upload encyrpted data for exfiltration.

T1020.subject: S9041
T1020.text: TeamPCP Cloud Stealer can compress and encrypt data and exfiltrate it via POST to scan.aquasecurtiy[.]org. If that method fails it attempts to use a stolen GITHUB_TOKEN to create a repo and exfiltrate the data there.

T1021.subject: G0102
T1021.text: Wizard Spider has used the WebDAV protocol to execute Ryuk payloads hosted on network file shares.

T1021.subject: G0143
T1021.text: Aquatic Panda used remote scheduled tasks to install malicious software on victim systems during lateral movement actions.

T1021.subject: G1003
T1021.text: Ember Bear uses valid network credentials gathered through credential harvesting to move laterally within victim networks, often employing the Impacket framework to do so.

T1021.subject: S0437
T1021.text: Kivars has the ability to remotely trigger keyboard input and mouse clicks.

T1021.subject: S0603
T1021.text: Stuxnet can propagate via peer-to-peer communication and updates using RPC.

T1021.subject: S1016
T1021.text: MacMa can manage remote screen sessions.

T1021.subject: S1063
T1021.text: Brute Ratel C4 has the ability to use RPC for lateral movement.

T1027.subject: C0015
T1027.text: During C0015, the threat actors used Base64-encoded strings.

T1027.subject: C0017
T1027.text: During C0017, APT41 broke malicious binaries, including DEADEYE and KEYPLUG, into multiple sections on disk to evade detection.

T1027.subject: C0025
T1027.text: During the 2016 Ukraine Electric Power Attack, Sandworm Team used heavily obfuscated code with Industroyer in its Windows Notepad backdoor.

T1027.subject: C0057
T1027.text: During the 3CX Supply Chain Attack, AppleJeus payloads use AES-256 GCM cipher to encrypt data to include ICONICSTEALER and VEILEDSIGNAL.

T1027.subject: G0004
T1027.text: Ke3chang has used Base64-encoded shellcode strings.

T1027.subject: G0022
T1027.text: APT3 obfuscates files or information to help evade defensive measures.

T1027.subject: G0034
T1027.text: Sandworm Team has used Base64 encoding within malware variants.

T1027.subject: G0047
T1027.text: Gamaredon Group has delivered self-extracting 7z archive files within malicious document attachments. Additionally, Gamaredon Group has used an obfuscated .drv file.

T1027.subject: G0063
T1027.text: BlackOasis's first stage shellcode contains a NOP sled with alternative instructions that was likely designed to bypass antivirus tools.

T1027.subject: G0067
T1027.text: APT37 obfuscates strings and payloads.

T1027.subject: G0084
T1027.text: Gallmaker obfuscated shellcode used during execution.

T1027.subject: G0093
T1027.text: GALLIUM used a modified version of HTRAN in which they obfuscated strings such as debug messages in an apparent attempt to evade detection.

T1027.subject: G0094
T1027.text: Kimsuky has obfuscated binary strings including the use of XOR encryption and Base64 encoding. Kimsuky has also modified the first byte of DLL implants targeting victims to prevent recognition of the executable file format. Kimsuky has obfuscated strings using Single Instruction Multiple Data (SIMD) instructions that complicate static analysis.

T1027.subject: G0096
T1027.text: APT41 used VMProtected binaries in multiple intrusions.

T1027.subject: G0099
T1027.text: APT-C-36 has used ConfuserEx to obfuscate its variant of Imminent Monitor, compressed payloads and RAT packages, and password protected encrypted email attachments to avoid detection. APT-C-36 has also compressed initial droppers into ZIP, LHA and UUE formats.

T1027.subject: G0106
T1027.text: Rocke has modified UPX headers after packing files to break unpackers.

T1027.subject: G0112
T1027.text: Windshift has used string encoding with floating point calculations.

T1027.subject: G0129
T1027.text: Mustang Panda has delivered initial payloads hidden using archives and encoding measures. Mustang Panda has also utilized opaque predicates in payloads to hinder analysis.

T1027.subject: G0135
T1027.text: BackdoorDiplomacy has obfuscated tools and malware it uses with VMProtect.

T1027.subject: G1006
T1027.text: Earth Lusca used Base64 to encode strings.

T1027.subject: G1036
T1027.text: Moonstone Sleet delivers encrypted payloads in pieces that are then combined together to form a new portable executable (PE) file during installation.

T1027.subject: G1039
T1027.text: RedCurl has used malware with string encryption. RedCurl has also encrypted data and has encoded PowerShell commands using Base64. RedCurl has used `PyArmor` to obfuscate code execution of LaZagne. Additionally, RedCurl has obfuscated downloaded files by renaming them as commonly used tools and has used `echo`, instead of file names themselves, to execute files.

T1027.subject: S0012
T1027.text: PoisonIvy hides any strings related to its own indicators of compromise.

T1027.subject: S0013
T1027.text: PlugX can use API hashing and modify the names of strings to evade detection.

T1027.subject: S0030
T1027.text: Carbanak encrypts strings to make analysis more difficult.

T1027.subject: S0045
T1027.text: Most of the strings in ADVSTORESHELL are encrypted with an XOR-based algorithm; some strings are also encrypted with 3DES and reversed. API function names are also reversed, presumably to avoid detection in memory.

T1027.subject: S0051
T1027.text: MiniDuke can use control flow flattening to obscure code.

T1027.subject: S0062
T1027.text: The DustySky dropper uses a function to obfuscate the name of functions and other parts of the malware.

T1027.subject: S0063
T1027.text: SHOTPUT is obscured using XOR encoding and appended to a valid GIF file.

T1027.subject: S0070
T1027.text: HTTPBrowser's code may be obfuscated through structured exception handling and return-oriented programming.

T1027.subject: S0091
T1027.text: Epic heavily obfuscates its code to make analysis more difficult.

T1027.subject: S0094
T1027.text: Trojan.Karagany can base64 encode and AES-128-CBC encrypt data prior to transmission.

T1027.subject: S0117
T1027.text: A version of XTunnel introduced in July 2015 obfuscated the binary using opaque predicates and other techniques in a likely attempt to obfuscate it and bypass security products.

T1027.subject: S0124
T1027.text: Pisloader obfuscates files by splitting strings into smaller sub-strings and including "garbage" strings that are never used. The malware also uses return-oriented programming (ROP) technique and single-byte XOR to obfuscate data.

T1027.subject: S0126
T1027.text: ComRAT has encrypted its virtual file system using AES-256 in XTS mode.

T1027.subject: S0132
T1027.text: H1N1 uses multiple techniques to obfuscate strings, including XOR.

T1027.subject: S0137
T1027.text: CORESHELL obfuscates strings using a custom stream cipher.

T1027.subject: S0138
T1027.text: OLDBAIT obfuscates internal strings and unpacks them at startup.

T1027.subject: S0140
T1027.text: Shamoon contains base64-encoded strings.

T1027.subject: S0142
T1027.text: StreamEx obfuscates some commands by using statically programmed fragments of strings when starting a DLL. It also uses a one-byte xor against 0x91 to encode configuration data.

T1027.subject: S0148
T1027.text: RTM strings, network data, configuration, and modules are encrypted with a modified RC4 algorithm.

T1027.subject: S0150
T1027.text: POSHSPY appends a file signature header (randomly selected from six file types) to encrypted data prior to upload or download.

T1027.subject: S0154
T1027.text: Cobalt Strike can hash functions to obfuscate calls to the Windows API and use a public/private key pair to encrypt Beacon session metadata.

T1027.subject: S0167
T1027.text: Matryoshka obfuscates API function names using a substitute cipher combined with Base64 encoding.

T1027.subject: S0182
T1027.text: FinFisher is heavily obfuscated in many ways, including through the use of spaghetti code in its functions in an effort to confuse disassembly programs. It also uses a custom XOR algorithm to obfuscate code.

T1027.subject: S0187
T1027.text: Daserf uses encrypted Windows APIs and also encrypts data using the alternative base64+RC4 or the Caesar cipher.

T1027.subject: S0189
T1027.text: ISMInjector is obfuscated with the off-the-shelf SmartAssembly .NET obfuscator created by red-gate.com.

T1027.subject: S0196
T1027.text: PUNCHBUGGY has hashed most its code's functions and encrypted payloads with base64 and XOR.

T1027.subject: S0197
T1027.text: PUNCHTRACK is loaded and executed by a highly obfuscated launcher.

T1027.subject: S0198
T1027.text: NETWIRE has used a custom obfuscation algorithm to hide strings including Registry keys, APIs, and DLL names.

T1027.subject: S0201
T1027.text: A JPIN uses a encrypted and compressed payload that is disguised as a bitmap within the resource section of the installer.

T1027.subject: S0203
T1027.text: Hydraq uses basic obfuscation in the form of spaghetti code.

T1027.subject: S0229
T1027.text: Some Orz strings are base64 encoded, such as the embedded DLL known as MockDll.

T1027.subject: S0240
T1027.text: ROKRAT can encrypt data prior to exfiltration by using an RSA public key.

T1027.subject: S0242
T1027.text: SynAck payloads are obfuscated prior to compilation to inhibit analysis and/or reverse engineering.

T1027.subject: S0244
T1027.text: Comnie uses RC4 and Base64 to obfuscate strings.

T1027.subject: S0259
T1027.text: InnaputRAT uses an 8-byte XOR key to obfuscate API names and other strings contained in the payload.

T1027.subject: S0260
T1027.text: InvisiMole avoids analysis by encrypting all strings, internal files, configuration data and by using a custom executable format.

T1027.subject: S0264
T1027.text: OopsIE uses the Confuser protector to obfuscate an embedded .Net Framework assembly used for C2. OopsIE also encodes collected data in hexadecimal format before writing to files on disk and obfuscates strings.

T1027.subject: S0265
T1027.text: Kazuar is obfuscated using the open source ConfuserEx protector. Kazuar also obfuscates the name of created files/folders/mutexes and encrypts debug messages written to log files using the Rijndael cipher.

T1027.subject: S0266
T1027.text: TrickBot uses non-descriptive names to hide functionality.

T1027.subject: S0283
T1027.text: jRAT’s Java payload is encrypted with AES. Additionally, backdoor files are encrypted using DES as a stream cipher. Later variants of jRAT also incorporated AV evasion methods such as Java bytecode obfuscation via the commercial Allatori obfuscation tool.

T1027.subject: S0331
T1027.text: Agent Tesla has had its code obfuscated in an apparent attempt to make analysis difficult. Agent Tesla has used the Rijndael symmetric encryption algorithm to encrypt strings.

T1027.subject: S0332
T1027.text: Remcos uses RC4 and base64 to obfuscate data, including Registry entries and file paths. Remcos can also employ control flow flattening to hinder analysis.

T1027.subject: S0335
T1027.text: Carbon encrypts configuration files and tasks for the malware to complete using CAST-128 algorithm.

T1027.subject: S0336
T1027.text: NanoCore’s plugins were obfuscated with Eazfuscater.NET 3.3.

T1027.subject: S0353
T1027.text: NOKKI uses Base64 encoding for strings.

T1027.subject: S0354
T1027.text: Denis obfuscates its code and encrypts the API names.

T1027.subject: S0355
T1027.text: Final1stspy obfuscates strings with base64 encoding.

T1027.subject: S0369
T1027.text: CoinTicker initially downloads a hidden encoded file.

T1027.subject: S0377
T1027.text: Ebury has obfuscated its strings with a simple XOR encryption with a static key.

T1027.subject: S0384
T1027.text: Dridex's strings are obfuscated using RC4.

T1027.subject: S0393
T1027.text: PowerStallion uses a XOR cipher to encrypt command output written to its OneDrive C2 server.

T1027.subject: S0428
T1027.text: PoetRAT has used a custom encryption scheme for communication between scripts.

T1027.subject: S0434
T1027.text: Imminent Monitor has encrypted the spearphish attachments to avoid detection from email gateways; the debugger also encrypts information before sending to the C2.

T1027.subject: S0445
T1027.text: ShimRatReporter encrypted gathered information with a combination of shifting and XOR using a static key.

T1027.subject: S0446
T1027.text: Ryuk can use anti-disassembly and code transformation obfuscation techniques.

T1027.subject: S0447
T1027.text: Lokibot has obfuscated strings with base64 encoding.

T1027.subject: S0449
T1027.text: Maze has decrypted strings and other important information during the encryption process. Maze also calls certain functions dynamically to hinder analysis.

T1027.subject: S0458
T1027.text: Ramsay has base64-encoded its portable executable and hidden itself under a JPG header. Ramsay can also embed information within document footers.

T1027.subject: S0461
T1027.text: SDBbot has the ability to XOR the strings for its installer component with a hardcoded 128 byte key.

T1027.subject: S0465
T1027.text: CARROTBALL has used a custom base64 alphabet to decode files.

T1027.subject: S0467
T1027.text: TajMahal has used an encrypted Virtual File System to store plugins.

T1027.subject: S0476
T1027.text: Valak has the ability to base64 encode and XOR encrypt strings.

T1027.subject: S0482
T1027.text: Bundlore has obfuscated data with base64, AES, RC4, and bz2.

T1027.subject: S0499
T1027.text: Hancitor has used Base64 to encode malicious links.

T1027.subject: S0500
T1027.text: MCMD can Base64 encode output strings prior to sending to C2.

T1027.subject: S0502
T1027.text: Drovorub has used XOR encrypted payloads in WebSocket client to server messages.

T1027.subject: S0504
T1027.text: Anchor has obfuscated code with stack strings and string encryption.

T1027.subject: S0511
T1027.text: RegDuke can use control-flow flattening or the commercially available .NET Reactor for obfuscation.

T1027.subject: S0512
T1027.text: FatDuke can use base64 encoding, string stacking, and opaque predicates for obfuscation.

T1027.subject: S0516
T1027.text: SoreFang has the ability to encode and RC6 encrypt data sent to C2.

T1027.subject: S0517
T1027.text: Pillowmint has obfuscated the AES key used for encryption.

T1027.subject: S0518
T1027.text: PolyglotDuke can custom encrypt strings.

T1027.subject: S0559
T1027.text: SUNBURST obfuscated collected system information using a FNV-1a + XOR algorithm.

T1027.subject: S0560
T1027.text: TEARDROP created and read from a file with a fake JPG header, and its payload was encrypted with a simple rotating XOR cipher.

T1027.subject: S0562
T1027.text: SUNSPOT encrypted log entries it collected with the stream cipher RC4 using a hard-coded key. It also uses AES128-CBC encrypted blobs for SUNBURST source code and data extracted from the SolarWinds Orion process.

T1027.subject: S0575
T1027.text: Conti can use compiler-based obfuscation for its code, encrypt DLLs, and hide Windows API calls.

T1027.subject: S0584
T1027.text: AppleJeus has XOR-encrypted collected system information prior to sending to a C2. AppleJeus has also used the open source ADVObfuscation library for its components.

T1027.subject: S0593
T1027.text: ECCENTRICBANDWAGON has encrypted strings with RC4.

T1027.subject: S0594
T1027.text: Out1 has the ability to encode data.

T1027.subject: S0596
T1027.text: ShadowPad has encrypted its payload, a virtual file system, and various files.

T1027.subject: S0598
T1027.text: P.A.S. Webshell can use encryption and base64 encoding to hide strings and to enforce access control once deployed.

T1027.subject: S0604
T1027.text: Industroyer uses heavily obfuscated code in its Windows Notepad backdoor.

T1027.subject: S0605
T1027.text: EKANS uses encoded strings in its process kill list.

T1027.subject: S0607
T1027.text: KillDisk uses VMProtect to make reverse engineering the malware more difficult.

T1027.subject: S0608
T1027.text: Conficker has obfuscated its code to prevent its removal from host machines.

T1027.subject: S0615
T1027.text: SombRAT can encrypt strings with XOR-based routines and use a custom AES storage format for plugins, configuration, C2 domains, and harvested data.

T1027.subject: S0622
T1027.text: AppleSeed has the ability to Base64 encode its payload and custom encrypt API calls.

T1027.subject: S0623
T1027.text: Siloscape itself is obfuscated and uses obfuscated API calls.

T1027.subject: S0624
T1027.text: Ecipekac can use XOR, AES, and DES to encrypt loader shellcode.

T1027.subject: S0625
T1027.text: Cuba has used multiple layers of obfuscation to avoid analysis, including its Base64 encoded payload.

T1027.subject: S0627
T1027.text: SodaMaster can use "stackstrings" for obfuscation.

T1027.subject: S0632
T1027.text: GrimAgent has used Rotate on Right (RoR) and Rotate on Left (RoL) functionality to encrypt strings.

T1027.subject: S0633
T1027.text: Sliver obfuscates configuration and other static files using native Go libraries such as `garble` and `gobfuscate` to inhibit configuration analysis and static detection.

T1027.subject: S0635
T1027.text: BoomBox can encrypt data using AES prior to exfiltration.

T1027.subject: S0640
T1027.text: Avaddon has used encrypted strings.

T1027.subject: S0641
T1027.text: Kobalos encrypts all strings using RC4 and bundles all functionality into a single function call.

T1027.subject: S0647
T1027.text: Turian can use VMProtect for obfuscation.

T1027.subject: S0650
T1027.text: QakBot has hidden code within Excel spreadsheets by turning the font color to white and splitting it across multiple cells.

T1027.subject: S0651
T1027.text: BoxCaon used the "StackStrings" obfuscation technique to hide malicious functionalities.

T1027.subject: S0659
T1027.text: Diavol has Base64 encoded the RSA public key used for encrypting files.

T1027.subject: S0660
T1027.text: The Clambling executable has been obfuscated when dropped on a compromised host.

T1027.subject: S0681
T1027.text: Lizar has obfuscated the fingerprint of the victim system, the local IP address, and the Fowler-Noll-V 1 (FNV-1) hash of the local IP address using an XOR operation. The data is then sent to the C2 server.

T1027.subject: S0690
T1027.text: Green Lambert has encrypted strings.

T1027.subject: S0694
T1027.text: DRATzarus can be partly encrypted with XOR.

T1027.subject: S0696
T1027.text: Flagpro has been delivered within ZIP or RAR password-protected archived files.

T1027.subject: S1018
T1027.text: Saint Bot has been obfuscated to help avoid detection.

T1027.subject: S1025
T1027.text: Amadey has obfuscated strings such as antivirus vendor names, domains, files, and others.

T1027.subject: S1028
T1027.text: Action RAT's commands, strings, and domains can be Base64 encoded within the payload.

T1027.subject: S1035
T1027.text: Small Sieve has the ability to use a custom hex byte swapping encoding scheme combined with an obfuscated Base64 function to protect program strings and Telegram credentials.

T1027.subject: S1039
T1027.text: Bumblebee has been delivered as password-protected zipped ISO files and used control-flow-flattening to obfuscate the flow of functions.

T1027.subject: S1053
T1027.text: AvosLocker has used XOR-encoded strings.

T1027.subject: S1063
T1027.text: Brute Ratel C4 has used encrypted payload files and maintains an encrypted configuration structure in memory.

T1027.subject: S1064
T1027.text: SVCReady can encrypt victim data with an RC4 cipher.

T1027.subject: S1066
T1027.text: DarkTortilla has been obfuscated with the DeepSea .NET and ConfuserEx code obfuscators.

T1027.subject: S1085
T1027.text: Sardonic can use certain ConfuserEx features for obfuscation and can be encoded in a base64 string.

T1027.subject: S1086
T1027.text: Snip3 has the ability to obfuscate strings using XOR encryption.

T1027.subject: S1090
T1027.text: NightClub can obfuscate strings using the congruential generator `(LCG): staten+1 = (690069 × staten + 1) mod 232`.

T1027.subject: S1099
T1027.text: Samurai can encrypt the names of requested APIs.

T1027.subject: S1104
T1027.text: SLOWPULSE can hide malicious code in the padding regions between legitimate functions in the Pulse Secure `libdsplibs.so` file.

T1027.subject: S1105
